output.title: Spot trial expiry before it becomes a surprise
output.body:
If you are running a small business, trial expiry is a simple workflow decision, not a grand AI project: when should a reminder fire, and who should see it first? The useful question is whether your trial dates already live in one place—calendar, email, spreadsheet, or CRM—or whether they are scattered across a few vendor accounts. If the dates are already central, a light monitoring rule may be enough. If they are scattered, you are probably looking at a small integration job, not a full overhaul.

The key control is human approval. Automation should surface the date; the owner still decides whether to renew, downgrade, or cancel. That matters because money movement and binding decisions should stay with a person. AI can help you notice the deadline, but it should not quietly choose the plan. That would be a very efficient way to buy the wrong thing.

A practical next step is to list every SaaS trial you are using and mark which tool, if any, already tracks the renewal date. That inventory tells you whether you need a simple reminder, a shared task, or a slightly smarter workflow in your own environment. Bareni’s approach starts with that one recurring workflow and keeps the decision bounded.
